docs.title: FastAPI SQLite CRUD Documentation
docs.text:
FastAPI SQLite CRUD Example is a production-minded backend portfolio project built with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, and JWT authentication. It demonstrates how to structure a small but realistic REST API with authentication, validation, testing, Docker support, and published documentation.

This documentation is intended for recruiters, developers, and collaborators who want to understand what the project does, how it is organized, and how to run or extend it locally.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• REST API development with FastAPI.
  • SQLite persistence with SQLAlchemy ORM.
  • JWT-based authentication for protected endpoints.
  • Pydantic schemas for validation and serialization.
  • Layered backend structure with routers, CRUD helpers, services, and configuration.
  • Automated testing with Pytest.
  • Docker-based local setup.
  • Documentation published with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs.

docs.title: Why it matters
docs.text: This project is designed to be small enough to review quickly and structured enough to show backend engineering habits beyond a minimal CRUD demo. For portfolio use, it highlights practical concerns such as authentication, organization, testing, documentation, and delivery workflow.

docs.title: API Usage
docs.text: This section shows a few typical request patterns for working with the API.

docs.title: Create an access token
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/token" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" ^
  -d "username=example&password=secret"

docs.title: List items
docs.text:
curl -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/" ^
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"

docs.title: Create an item
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" ^
  -d '{"title":"Example item","description":"Created from API usage example"}'

docs.title: Suggested usage
docs.text: For interactive exploration, use Swagger UI at /docs. For quick manual verification during development, curl examples like the ones above are usually enough.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The project uses a layered FastAPI structure that separates routing, schemas, persistence, and service logic. This keeps the codebase easier to test, extend, and explain.

docs.title: High-level layout
docs.text:
app/
├── routers/          # API route modules
├── auth.py           # Authentication helpers and token logic
├── config.py         # Application settings
├── crud.py           # Data access helpers
├── database.py       # Engine and session management
├── logging_utils.py  # Logging configuration
├── main.py           # FastAPI application entry point
├── models.py         # SQLAlchemy ORM models
├── schemas.py        # Pydantic request/response schemas
└── services.py       # Service-layer business logic

docs.title: main.py
docs.text: Creates the FastAPI application, registers middleware and routers, and exposes the application entry point used by Uvicorn.

docs.title: routers/
docs.text: Defines HTTP endpoints and request/response behavior. Routers should stay thin and delegate business logic to lower layers when possible.

docs.title: schemas.py
docs.text: Contains Pydantic models for request validation and response serialization. This keeps API contracts explicit and helps separate transport models from database models.

docs.title: models.py
docs.text: Defines SQLAlchemy ORM models used for persistence in SQLite.

docs.title: crud.py
docs.text: Encapsulates common database operations such as create, read, update, and delete.

docs.title: services.py
docs.text: Provides a place for business rules and orchestration logic that should not live directly in routes.

docs.title: auth.py
docs.text: Handles authentication utilities such as password verification, hashing, token creation, and user authentication flow.

docs.title: database.py
docs.text: Creates the SQLAlchemy engine and session dependency used by the application.

docs.title: logging_utils.py
docs.text: Supports structured and security-aware logging so important runtime and auth events can be traced more clearly.

docs.title: Why this structure works
docs.text: This structure is appropriate for a small-to-medium backend project because it avoids putting all logic into one file while remaining simple enough to follow quickly. For portfolio purposes, it also makes architectural decisions visible to reviewers.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The project uses JWT-based authentication to protect selected API routes.

docs.title: Authentication flow
docs.text:
1. A user submits credentials to the login endpoint.
  2. The application verifies the credentials.
  3. If authentication succeeds, the server returns a JWT access token.
  4. The client sends the token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
  5. Protected endpoints validate the token before granting access.

docs.title: Typical login request
docs.text:
POST /token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=example&password=secret

docs.title: Typical authenticated request
docs.text:
GET /items/
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Passwords should be stored as hashes, not plain text.
  • Tokens should only be issued after successful credential verification.
  • Protected endpoints should reject missing, invalid, or expired tokens.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide shows how to run the project locally for development and testing.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Make sure you have the following installed:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Git
  • Optional: Docker and Docker Compose

docs.title: Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/antoniooreany/fastapi-sqlite-crud.git
cd fastapi-sqlite-crud

docs.title: Windows PowerShell
docs.text:
python -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

docs.title: Linux/macOS
docs.text:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Install dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Run the application
docs.text:
uvicorn app.main:app --reload

When the server starts, open:

  • http://127.0.0.1:8000/ — frontend
  • http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs — Swagger UI
  • http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc — ReDoc

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
pytest

Verbose output:

pytest -v

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text: docker-compose up --build

docs.title: Build and deploy documentation
docs.text:
Build docs locally:

mkdocs build

Serve docs locally:

mkdocs serve

Deploy docs to GitHub Pages:

mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Testing and Quality
docs.text: The project includes several practices intended to make the codebase easier to validate and maintain.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Automated tests are executed with Pytest:

pytest

Use verbose mode when needed:

pytest -v

docs.title: Quality practices
docs.text:
• Typed request and response schemas with Pydantic.
  • Layered backend organization for clarity and maintainability.
  • JWT authentication for protected routes.
  • Structured logging for debugging and operational visibility.
  • Docker support for reproducible local setup.
  • MkDocs documentation for onboarding and review.

docs.title: Git workflow
docs.text:
This repository uses a simple long-lived branch model:

  • main — stable, release-ready branch.
  • develop — integration branch for ongoing work.
  • gh-pages — documentation deployment branch.

Short-lived branches are created from develop:

  • feature/<name>
  • fix/<name>
  • docs/<name>

Normal work is merged into develop through Pull Requests. Release-ready changes are then promoted from develop to main.
